headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: unstructured can read/write and egress allowlisted data while pathway is a non-writing document processor, so the pair can move documents into downstream actions with limited isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway has no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or stdin/stdout surfaces, so it cannot directly inject into Unstructured. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer of document content into Unstructured’s file inputs, which is an unusual configuration and not a default shared channel. Uncertainty is low because both profiles show no direct inter-agent channel.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Pathway-produced text into Unstructured document inputs, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem is introduced between the agents, the pathway changes from manual to direct.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted Pathway output into Unstructured prompts or templates.
Use a human review step before any content from Pathway is fed to Unstructured.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared mount if added later.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pathway touches no data classes and has no egress, but Unstructured reads files, processes documents/images/text, and can call allowlisted external APIs. If both are pointed at the same workspace, documents can flow from Pathway into Unstructured and then out to third-party services. This is a default-capable leakage path, though not proven for secrets specifically.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same document workspace, Unstructured can ingest Pathway-produced files.
IF Unstructured is configured to use its allowlisted API calls on those documents, content may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Separate input/output directories for the two agents.
Restrict Unstructured to local-only processing where possible.
Review allowlisted endpoints before processing sensitive documents.
Run a quick test with a non-sensitive file to confirm no unintended uploads.
Delete intermediate files after each run.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with Unstructured. Unstructured can write the filesystem and supports multiple instances, but the pair lacks overlapping write authority on the same resource in the profiles. The conflict pathway is therefore limited unless an operator adds a shared writable target.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator routes both agents to the same mutable artifact, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator step.
Use file locks on any shared artifact.
Avoid sharing git working trees between the agents.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pathway is a document-processing system and Unstructured is also a document processor that can read files and emit downstream outputs. If Unstructured treats Pathway output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade across multiple work products. The profiles do not show explicit verification or critique steps, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Pathway output is fed into Unstructured as source material, downstream errors can propagate.
IF Unstructured is used to generate deliverables without a verification step, incorrect structure or extraction can be amplified.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Pathway and Unstructured.
Compare a sample of outputs against source documents.
Require human approval before downstream publication.
Log provenance for each transformed document.

E_compliance.rationale: Pathway’s profile shows no touched data classes or external calls, while Unstructured explicitly processes documents, images, and text and exposes privacy-policy/docs endpoints. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch around retention or residency if sensitive documents are routed through Unstructured. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are processed by Unstructured, its documented external endpoints and retention rules become relevant.
IF the operator requires stricter residency or retention than Unstructured provides, a compliance gap exists.
mitigations: Review Unstructured privacy and retention terms before use.
Avoid sending regulated documents through the pair.
Keep a local-only processing path for sensitive files.
Document the data flow for audit purposes.
